evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Continuously improve our analytics platform through robust modeling, testing, documentation, and engineering best practices
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour signals dominate — 'robust modeling, testing, documentation, and engineering best practices' plus 'trusted data foundations', with no shipping-speed language in the responsibilities.
evidence.domain_risk: Build and maintain scalable, production-grade data models and analytics foundations that power decision-making across our 7 international markets
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate — errors affect product and business decision-making across markets, but the JD names no financial reporting, audit or regulatory exposure.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Continuously improve our analytics platform through robust modeling, testing, documentation, and engineering best practices
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid — an analytics platform, production data models and named stack (BigQuery, Looker, dbt/Dataform/SQLMesh) already exist and the role extends them, but no specialised data sub-teams are described.
evidence.jd_authorship: Enable self-service analytics through trusted metrics, reusable semantic models, and scalable data products
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Mixed — some precise bullets ('reusable semantic models', 'across our 7 international markets') sit alongside boilerplate like 'turn data into actionable insights'.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Partner with Product Managers and business stakeholders to define success metrics, evaluate product outcomes, and turn data into actionable insights
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Product — the only named partner function is Product Managers and the work is framed around evaluating product outcomes and success metrics.
evidence.autonomy_level: define success metrics ... Continuously improve our analytics platform
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Mixed — the candidate owns the analytics platform's improvement and helps 'define success metrics', but the overall framing is enablement of other teams rather than setting direction.
evidence.ai_role: Leverage AI and modern analytics tooling to accelerate insight generation, improve analytics workflows
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_user — the candidate is expected to use AI tooling to speed up their own analytics workflow, not to build data foundations that AI systems consume.
evidence.testing_framing: Continuously improve our analytics platform through robust modeling, testing, documentation, and engineering best practices
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility — testing appears as an owned, ongoing responsibility bullet with the action verb 'continuously improve', not as a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate — trust and trustworthiness appear repeatedly ('trusted metrics', 'accessible and trustworthy') but as an enablement aspiration, with no compliance, audit or incident risk register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Build and maintain scalable, production-grade data models ... Continuously improve our analytics platform
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mixed — 'build' new data products sits alongside 'maintain' and 'continuously improve' an existing analytics platform.
evidence.work_arrangement: You work remotely (Germany-wide), with offices in Hamburg, Berlin or Munich
evidence.loss_aversion: 'We are looking for an Analytics Engineer who enjoys building trusted data foundations' — trust in data is the stated motivation, but framed as enablement rather than risk avoidance.
